title: indigo_libs: add AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY with aux_simulator as the reference driver
description:
Add the AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY standard property and make aux_simulator the reference driver.

- indigo_libs: AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY property and item names (SAFE, CLOUDS, RAIN, WIND, HUMIDITY) in indigo_names.h; one shared helper in indigo_aux_driver.c that evaluates the conditions (per condition: fitted or not, valid reading or not, unsafe level reached or not) into the lights and the reason message, so every driver behaves the same. No generator change: drivers declare the property in their .driver files like AUX_WEATHER.
- aux_simulator: it already has AUX_CLOUD, AUX_RAIN and AUX_WIND with fixed limits. Add AUX_CLOUD_THRESHOLDS, AUX_RAIN_THRESHOLDS, AUX_WIND_THRESHOLDS, AUX_HUMIDITY_THRESHOLDS and AUX_HUMIDITY, drive the classification from them, and add AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY. Bump the driver version.
- indigo_docs/PROPERTIES.md: the new property and the simulator's new properties; document the safety rule in the aux section.
- Tests: integration tests on the simulator for every condition crossing its unsafe level and back, SAFE combining, the reason message, Idle when disconnected, threshold changes taking effect, a condition switched off by an out-of-reach threshold; unit tests for the helper if practical.


Agreed design (owner, 2026-11-23):

New standard light property AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY (read-only) on weather devices, items SAFE, CLOUDS, RAIN, WIND, HUMIDITY. Every weather driver defines all five items.
- Condition item: Idle = no such sensor in the driver or none fitted on this unit; Ok = reading below its unsafe level; Alert = reading at or past its unsafe level, or a fitted sensor gives no valid reading (a broken sensor is never Idle).
- SAFE: Alert as soon as any condition is Alert; Ok when every fitted sensor is Ok; Idle when no condition has a sensor or the device is disconnected.
- The reason is given in the update message when the verdict changes, e.g. "Unsafe: wind 12.4 m/s above 10.0 m/s" or "Safe: all conditions within limits"; the measured values stay in AUX_WEATHER and the condition lights show which limit was crossed.

Unsafe levels reuse the existing standard two-level classification and threshold properties (as in aux_cloudwatcher): AUX_CLOUD_THRESHOLDS / AUX_CLOUD, AUX_RAIN_THRESHOLDS / AUX_RAIN, AUX_WIND_THRESHOLDS / AUX_WIND, AUX_HUMIDITY_THRESHOLDS / AUX_HUMIDITY. The worst level is unsafe: clouds OVERCAST, rain RAINING, wind STRONG, humidity HUMID. Each driver sets its own threshold defaults in its own units. A condition is switched off by moving its unsafe threshold out of reach; no extra limits or enable property.

Powerboxes (ppb, upb, upb3, usbdp, mgbox, svbpowerbox, wbplusv3, wbprov3) are excluded: they control dew heaters. sqm, astromechanics and mount_lx200 are excluded: they measure none of the four conditions.

Tickets: (1) framework + aux_simulator, (2) aux_cloudwatcher, (3) aux_skyalert, (4) system_alpaca, (5) agent_auxiliary aggregation. 2-5 depend on 1.

outcome.summary:
Independent review of master...HEAD (ce1c74aad). Verdict: pass.

Verified:
- Design and owner notes met: AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY items SAFE/CLOUDS/RAIN/WIND/HUMIDITY (indigo_names.h:946-951); Idle without sensor, Alert for unsafe or invalid fitted sensor, property state Alert on invalid reading (indigo_aux_driver.c:95-127); SAFE rule (Alert wins, Ok when every fitted Ok, Idle when none fitted); connection-only definition in the generated connect handler (indigo_aux_simulator.c:589-590, deleted 627-628); thresholds always defined and saved via CONFIG (enumerate 793-796, save 819-824); worst level unsafe (severity == 2); simulator cloud classification on sky temperature as in aux_cloudwatcher (OVERCAST when not below CLOUDY, defaults -10/0); reason on verdict change and, while unsafe, on change of the ALERT set or of reading validity.
- Helper: message assembly is bounded (weather_safety_append uses vsnprintf with the remaining size and skips when full; unit test covers a 12-byte buffer), items looked up by name and missing items ignored, NULL/0 message buffer supported for the initial evaluation. Stateless: previous lights/state of the property are the previous result; callers must run it on the device queue like any property update (standard INDIGO convention). API fits cloudwatcher (reversed flag, fitted known after connect) and skyalert.
- Generated code: regenerated indigo_aux_simulator.driver in a temp dir with the unchanged build/bin/indigo_generator; .c, .h and _main.c are byte-identical to the checked-in files. No generator change, version 1 -> 2 (DRIVER_VERSION 0x03000002), no MAX_DEVICES override, no on_connect return, no finalizers, threshold on_change blocks only reclassify while connected.
- Behaviour changes vs master documented in PROPERTIES.md: wet threshold 0.1 mm/h instead of > 0, cloud classification by sky temperature instead of ambient-sky delta, new AUX_HUMIDITY and four threshold properties, AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY. Standard names, no X_ prefix needed.
-

Re-review of tree 355d8392 (commit 0596e5a99) after the recorded test run. The previous independent code review passed ce1c74aad (tree 0c6228dd); this review covers the delta and confirms the overall diff.
- git diff ce1c74aad HEAD --stat: only TEST_SUMMARY.md (+1) and indigo_drivers/aux_simulator/README.md (+1). The master...HEAD stat lists the same 10 files as before (indigo_libs names/helper, aux_simulator .driver/.c, PROPERTIES.md, integration and unit tests, plus the two record files). Nothing else changed.
- README: one line appended to the existing ## Testing section, "- 2026-11-23 01:53 3.0.0.2 linux x64 simulator 18/18 OK". The version matches DRIVER_VERSION 0x03000002 / .driver version = 2. 18 matches the 18 cases in the tests[] table of indigo_test/integration/test_aux_simulator.c. The existing mac arm64 simulator line is a different configuration, so it stays (indigo_test/AGENTS.md "keep only the latest run of each configuration"). Lines are in timestamp order and the format follows the AGENTS.md record form.
- TEST_SUMMARY.md: the only change is the matching aux_simulator row "| | 2026-11-23 01:53 | 3.0.0.2 | linux x64 | simulator | 18 / 18 | OK |", placed right after the existing aux_simulator row. Running python3 tools/make_test_summary.py -o - on the worktree produces output byte-identical to the committed TEST_SUMMARY.md, so it was generated rather than edited by hand, and no other rows changed.
- The whitespace and unit flow checks passed on tree 355d8392. The worktree is clean.
Verdict: pass. Limits: the test run itself was not repeated; this review relies on the recorded result and on the earlier code review of the unchanged product files.

history.text: Writing the AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY helper in indigo_aux_driver
Adding thresholds, AUX_HUMIDITY and AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY to aux_simulator.driver
Writing weather safety integration tests in test_aux_simulator.c

Implementer verification: flow check whitespace+unit passed (test_aux_math 7/7 incl. 5 new helper cases). test_aux_simulator 18/18 passed (5 new weather_safety cases), also its ASAN/UBSan build and 3 repeat runs; tools/run_driver_test.py aux_simulator --dry-run: 18/18 OK, not recorded in README/TEST_SUMMARY (owner decision pending). Runs need LD_LIBRARY_PATH unset: the session exports the primary checkout's build/lib, which shadows the worktree libindigo (RUNPATH) and fails with an undefined indigo_aux_evaluate_weather_safety. Limitation: the generator initialises AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY with state OK and on_attach runs before property allocation, so before the first connect the property state is OK (lights IDLE); after a disconnect indigo_aux_reset_weather_safety() sets state IDLE.

Owner decisions 2026-11-23 after the first implementation: (1) AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY is defined only while the device is connected, like AUX_WEATHER, and deleted on disconnect; the 'Idle when disconnected' case disappears (SAFE is still Idle when no condition has a sensor). The thresholds stay always defined and saved. (2) A fitted sensor with no valid reading sets its condition and SAFE Alert and the property state Alert (as implemented). (3) The simulator follows the Cloudwatcher meaning of AUX_CLOUD_THRESHOLDS: sky temperature in C, CLEAR when below CLEAR, CLOUDY when below CLOUDY, OVERCAST when not below CLOUDY (not reversed); pick defaults that fit the simulator's sky temperature input. (4) The reason message is sent when the SAFE verdict changes and also whenever the set of unsafe conditions (or no-valid-reading conditions) changes.
Rework per owner answers: connection-only property, reason-set messages, sky temperature clouds
Running test_aux_math and test_aux_simulator after rework

Rework after owner answers: AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY is connection-only in aux_simulator (lights set with indigo_aux_evaluate_weather_safety in on_connect, defined by the generated connect handler, deleted on disconnect); indigo_aux_reset_weather_safety removed. Reason message on SAFE change and, while unsafe, on any change of the ALERT condition set or of reading validity (property state). Simulator AUX_CLOUD_THRESHOLDS now sky temperature as in cloudwatcher, defaults CLEAR -10, CLOUDY 0. flow check passed on tree 0c6228dd (test_aux_math 8/8); test_aux_simulator 18/18 incl. ASAN; run_driver_test.py aux_simulator --dry-run 18/18 OK, not recorded. Known limit: stateless change detection misses a condition switching between unsafe and no-valid-reading while another condition stays without a valid reading.
Reviewer: building and running test_aux_math, test_aux_simulator, run_driver_test dry-run

Owner decision 2026-11-23: the known message gap of the stateless helper (a condition switching between unsafe and no valid reading while another fitted condition stays without a valid reading sends no new message; lights and verdict stay correct) is accepted. Do not add driver-kept state for it.

Non-blocking observations (no change requested):
1. Known gap (unsafe <-> no-valid-reading switch while another condition stays invalid gives no new message): low severity, lights and verdict stay correct, only the reason text is stale; accepted by the owner.
2. For ticket 4 (system_alpaca): an Alpaca SafetyMonitor exposes only IsSafe. indigo_aux_evaluate_weather_safety() derives SAFE solely from the four conditions, so a SAFE-only verdict cannot be expressed without mapping it onto a condition or setting the SAFE light directly; that ticket will have to decide (or extend the helper).
3. The verdict change to IDLE emits "Unknown: no weather condition is monitored" (indigo_aux_driver.c:160), which PROPERTIES.md does not quote; harmless.
4. If a driver omitted the SAFE item, the helper would report a verdict change on every non-idle evaluation; the design requires all five items, so not a defect.
